purpose: Bella Clip Name and missing-PMR-master requirements review. The user approved the unique-master selection and missing-name rule on 2026-10-19. No Bella implementation; OldScanner, BinFilter, KelpieId and physical inventory rules unchanged.

mediaComposer.scope: Bounded read-only static arm64 trace of native cached Clip Name lookup and the PMR version1 missing-master recovery route. No application launch, private API execution, database/media writes or Bella implementation.
keyConclusions: The ordinary native GetClipName path asks for the cached master association, resolves that exact master identity through the mob manager, then copies that object's component name. It does not guess a name from filenames or another Name attribute.

Concrete graph-based missing-master recovery exists in ReadPmrRec specifically for version1, whose stored record omits MasterMobId. It enumerates already-loaded type2 masters, visits their own components, and finds one whose source clips directly reference the target identity.
That version1 recovery stops at the first matching master in the typed mob-manager iteration. It does not count all distinct candidates or prove that the association is unique.

The traced component walk follows track/sequence containment and attached precompute components. At each source clip, the callback resolves its SourceID once; it does not recurse through arbitrary referenced mobs' track graphs.
This proves a native relationship route, not an automatic on-demand MDB opening mechanism or a universal repair for missing/null modern PMR master IDs.

Bella's proposed unique-candidate recovery is deliberately more conservative than the traced native version1 first-match behavior. It remains a product choice, not an existing approved selection rule.

recommendationForBella: When an explicit PMR MasterMobId is usable, resolve that exact complete identity to the corresponding qualified MDB master and read its own Clip Name.

When no usable explicit association is available, a conservative proposed fallback is to collect distinct qualified masters whose own supported track/component graph directly references the target full FileMobId.
Count distinct complete MasterMobIds, rather than tracks, source clips or repeated object records.

Use a recovered association only when exactly one candidate is established and the required graph is readable; multiple candidates or incomplete required relationships should leave Clip Name unavailable under the proposed basic release-one policy.

Do not select by filename, matching names, object order, an arbitrary Name attribute or a recursively discovered ancestor master. Do not copy the native v1 hash-iteration first-match tie-break as if it established uniqueness.
These selection/fallback recommendations are not implementation and are not newly approved by this research.
limits: Static current-Mac native trace only; no live v1/ambiguous/missing-master experiment.
The v1 branch is proven. No equivalent universal recovery path was established for a null modern PMR master or every Media Tool/UI call site.
No claim that the loaded mob manager contains only the current MDB; native recovery may see other loaded objects. Bella's catalogue scope must be explicit.
Native component traversal includes attached precomputes. Bella should qualify supported relationships deliberately and must not describe an unsupported or partially read graph as complete.
No production or media changes.

mdvx.scope: Read-only static ordinary PMR-referenced MDB scanner/enrichment path and corresponding table column display. No MDVx app launch or scan, source edits or media mutation. Existing binary hash reverified this turn.
conclusions: MDVx does not derive or select an MDB master when the supplied PMR MasterMobId fails lookup in the inspected ordinary row path.

It extracts8bytes atoffset16 of PMR MasterMobId, looks up the CompositionMobs index, and reads a name only from that matching object. It does not choose the first available MDB master or search a source graph for ClipName.
The PMR item parser supports versions2,8,16; it has no version1 record path that supplies a missing MasterMobId. Do not describe v1 as a supported master-inference case.

For a zero-filled masterID, the enrichment routine performs an ordinary zero8bytekey lookup without a special null-ID fallback. If no matching entry exists, master metadata is skipped; it does not choose an arbitrary master.

A newly created row with no master name normally shows the ... placeholder in ClipName. Filename is a separate column. A present empty string can display blank; no filename substitution exists in these column paths.
MDB string decoding here is the generic ASCII-if-II/MacRoman-otherwise route. This is not the database browser UTF8 path or Bella approved text decoding.

actualDatabases.purpose: Independent read-only candidate master graph review from actual raw MDB values, restricted to2412 sibling PMR file identities. No production reader/projector used.
method: Read complete MOBJ IDs; bridge only known organization42 legacy12 IDs.
Use HEAD local references and ObjectSpine membership, not12byte MobIndex identity equality or arbitrary file object order.
Candidate masters are catalogue CompositionMobs with usage7 or1 and no PhysicalMedia descriptor.
Walk only recorded track/component references to SCLP SourceID. Record direct file matches and separately follow uniquely resolved onward mob IDs for indirect matches.
A physical file identity is the stopping point; do not follow through its earlier original-source ancestry.
Compare the recorded PMR master against graph-derived candidates, without using that PMR master to construct the candidate set.
limits: Corpus is six genuine little-endian MDBs, not a universal format proof.
Known files in this review are the2412 physical-media entries already identified by PMR; no directory/header-only files are introduced.
Candidate counts are observations; they do not approve an arbitrary winner if a future file has multiple candidates.
Unresolved onward source IDs may describe unavailable original-source endpoints; reported separately from malformed local references.
Clip names are checked for presence/emptiness only. No arbitrary user attributes, source text or lyrics are copied.

aggregateExperiment.method: Withhold PMR MasterMobId during candidate derivation; use independent MDB own-track/source references, then compare against the recorded PMR master. Actual PMRs all store MasterMobId, so this is not a genuine missing-master or v1 runtime trial.
aggregateExperiment.result: All2412 target file IDs resolve to exactly one direct qualified master, and all match the recorded PMR master.
aggregateExperiment.qualification: The component routes and source-ID normalization are bounded by the supported inspected layouts. No actual ambiguous-master or malformed-local-graph case was exercised.

proposedBellaRule.status: Approved requirement on 2026-10-19; not implemented. The key name is retained from the research proposal.
proposedBellaRule.explicitMaster: When PMR supplies a usable MasterMobId, look up that full normalized identity on its catalogue-qualified master; read the exact Clip Name property. Do not broadly traverse to rediscover a supplied association.
proposedBellaRule.missingMaster: When PMR supplies no usable MasterMobId, use complete-ID source references from a qualified master own track/component graph to the target FileMobId. Count distinct full MasterMobIds.
proposedBellaRule.uniqueCandidate: Use the complete recovered MasterMobId and its own name only when exactly one candidate is established from readable relationships.
proposedBellaRule.noOrMultipleOrIncomplete: Leave MDB-derived master association/name unavailable when there is no candidate, more than one distinct candidate, or insufficient readable relationships. No arbitrary first/name/date/object-order tie-break.
proposedBellaRule.explicitButUnmatched: Keep a supplied PMR identity if MDB cannot resolve it. Do not silently select a different master. Additional source/header reads remain separately undecided.
proposedBellaRule.name: Read selected master CPNT:Name in observed legacy layout, appropriate MOBJ:Name in the corresponding supported layout; apply approved text rules. A missing/empty name does not select a different master.
proposedBellaRule.display: Propose empty Clip Name when unavailable; Filename remains separate. No new UI column is requested.
proposedBellaRule.coherence: Use the same selected master for other master-level metadata; no mixing names/classification from different masters.
scope: Exact supported own track/component source relationship; no association from shared source ancestry alone.
Native attached-precompute visitation is proven; actual CPNT:Precomputed values are zero in this corpus. Supported component alternatives must be deliberately qualified.
No newly mandatory header read, cross-source precedence rule or BinFilter change.
No need to retain a complete raw MDB graph as lasting scan output; no performance claim.

limits: No app launch, altered database, production source change or Bella implementation.
Native PMR-v1 first-match path was statically traced; it is not proof of a universal modern missing-master recovery or every MediaComposer UI display.
MDVx ordinary PMR-referenced MDB enrichment is distinguished from optional no-MDB header and unreferenced/AMA routes.
All genuine source files use little-endian metadata.
Sample uniqueness does not make multiple masters impossible; the proposed release-one rule deliberately leaves that case unavailable.

userDecision.response: Sounds good. Where do we go from here?
userDecision.approved: Use the explicit PMR MasterMobId when supplied; otherwise recover only one distinct qualified master from readable direct component/source links to the full FileMobId. Leave unavailable for no/multiple/insufficient candidates, retain physical row, and keep Filename separate. Select master before reading its name; do not switch for an empty name.
userDecision.scope: Requirements review only. Extra media-header reads, source precedence, remaining MDB structure/damage decisions and Bella implementation remain later work.
